78683.subject: Schwab Is Bringing AVAX to Traditional Investors
78683.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/schwab-is-bringing-avax-to-traditional

On August 27, Charles Schwab announced plans to add Solana, Avalanche, and Chainlink alongside Bitcoin and Ethereum.
For AVAX, the move puts the token in front of a huge audience of traditional investors. As of July 31, Schwab had $13.04 trillion in client assets across 39.9 million active accounts. Soon, eligible clients will be able to buy and sell AVAX alongside their stocks, ETFs, and other investments.
An audience of that size is significant on its own. But Schwab’s selection of Avalanche is also notable: the brokerage chose AVAX as part of its first expansion beyond BTC and ETH.
So why Avalanche?
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Avalanche Was Already on Wall Street’s Radar
Schwab hasn’t published a detailed breakdown of its selection criteria, saying only that the additions match client demand for established assets. Avalanche’s history with major financial institutions provides some useful context.
In November 2023, J.P. Morgan’s Onyx division and Apollo Global Management ran a Project Guardian proof of concept [ https://substack.com/redirect/f654aa10-7abc-4621-b7bb-8f12ec4f4e53?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] using a permissioned Avalanche Evergreen subnet, the predecessor to today’s Avalanche L1 architecture. WisdomTree provided tokenized funds for the trial, which tested how smart contracts could automate portfolio management across traditional and alternative assets. A few months later, in February 2024, Citi ran another trial on Avalanche Spruce [ https://substack.com/redirect/ae47ea09-ec87-457f-8def-28c41363b806?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] with Wellington Management and WisdomTree to test tokenized private funds, automated distribution rules, and compliance.
These were early pilots rather than full-scale products, and they happened years ago. Wall Street didn’t migrate to Avalanche overnight. What the trials did show, however, was that Avalanche was already attracting serious attention from major financial institutions.
Why Institutions Want Their Own L1
One of Avalanche’s main advantages for financial institutions is its customizable L1 architecture.
Financial firms may not want to run regulated assets on an open, shared public chain where fees can change and access can’t easily be restricted. An Avalanche L1 lets an institution set its own validator rules, restrict network access, and customize gas mechanics while remaining connected to the broader ecosystem.
Project Guardian showed how this could work in practice. The participants tested tokenized funds on a permissioned Avalanche network while maintaining control over who could take part. 🧠 Crypto News Brief: Crypto is on hold for the Senate's CLARITY Act cloture vote as Democrats counter a Trump-backed ethics deal. Bitcoin cools near $77K while Washington pushes crypto tax rules and sanctions enforcement. 🏛️ Democrats Send Counteroffer Hours Before CLARITY Act Cloture Vote Senate Democrats delivered a counterproposal to Republicans late Monday, a day after GOP negotiators released a “final” CLARITY Act draft with ethics restrictions President Trump agreed to accept. Democrats still object that state attorneys general could not sue the president directly and that ethics officials could grant waivers for crypto business ties. The procedural vote, which needs 60 senators, is set for 2:15 p.m. ET today. Read full story 📉 Bitcoin Retreats From $79.5K as Traders Brace for Senate Vote Bitcoin slipped to roughly $77,400 in European hours, giving back about 3% from an overnight peak near $79,530 and trading lower on the week. XRP bucked the trend with a gain of more than 2% to $1.41, while zcash rose nearly 3%. A Siebert Financial analyst argued the market may be overestimating how much the vote’s outcome matters. More details ⚖️ DOJ Moves to Seize $61M in Crypto Tied to Iranian Oil Sales Federal prosecutors in New York filed a civil forfeiture complaint targeting $61 million in crypto allegedly linked to Iran’s black-market oil trade and the IRGC. The funds are described as part of a $1.5 billion pipeline routed through unhosted wallets, with two Chinese firms allegedly using Binance accounts to launder proceeds. Binance said it does not permit transactions with sanctioned parties and is cooperating with authorities. Read more 🧾 House Panel Unveils 114-Page Crypto Tax Bill Ahead of Markup The House Ways and Means Committee released the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, covering de minimis transactions, wash sales, mining, staking and broker rules. It would exempt network or transaction fees under $10 from tax, excluding anyone with more than 5,000 transfers in the prior year. The committee votes on Sept. 16, though enactment this year looks unlikely. See details 🔒 Trump-Linked $800M WLFI Stake Locked Until 2028 On-chain data shows a World Liberty Financial token allocation matching President Trump’s disclosed holding entered a vesting contract in May after a mandatory 10% burn. A two-year cliff means the earliest unlock falls in 202
